item.title: Tom Jackson, former Broncos star and sports broadcaster, dies at 75
item.description: Former football star and famed broadcaster Tom Jackson has died, his family and ESPN announced Sunday. Jackson rose to prominence as a Denver Broncos player and went on to build a career as a beloved NFL analyst for ESPN, becoming a mainstay of the network's Sunday football programs for three decades, including its "Sunday NFL Countdown" show. He was 75. Jimmy Pitaro, the chairman of ESPN, praised Jackson in a statement released by the network after his death. In it, Pitaro called Jackson "one of the most influential and beloved figures in ESPN's history," who "brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans." "Alongside Chris Berman, he helped make NFL Primetime an iconic part of our football weekends," Pitaro said. "Away from the set, Tom was a trusted colleague, generous mentor and dear friend to many. We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him. His legacy at ESPN, throughout the NFL and among the countless fans who admired his incredible work will endure." Jackson's family informed ESPN that he died Friday, but it was their wish that his death not be announced until the start of the network's "Sunday NFL Countdown" show by Jackson's longtime friend and on-air partner Chris Berman. "Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst. There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him. And when it came to laughter, Tom's was frequent and unmistakable," Berman said at the start of the show. "Tom was my best friend professionally and personally. If you ever met him or just knew him from watching ESPN, he was your best friend, too." Berman said Jackson made a surprise visit a couple of weeks ago to ESPN, where he worked for 32 years after playing 14 seasons for the Broncos, and that the two talked on Tuesday. A fourth-round draft pick out of Louisville in 1973, Jackson was the inspirational leader of Denver's first Super Bowl team in 1977. He started 177 games for the Broncos between 1973-86, retiring after the team's second Super Bowl appearance. He was a two-time Associated Press All-Pro and three-time Pro Bowler. Following his playing days, Jackson had a second career at ESPN from 1987-2016 and was featured on "Sunday NFL Countdown" and "NFL Primetime." Before the internet and NBC took over the Sunday night package in 2006, "NFL Primetime" was must-see viewing for fans and players because it showed highlights from all the games, as well as the interplay between Berman and Jackson, who often finished each other's sentences. item.title: ‘Shocking’: Draymond Green says it’s ‘crazy’ after watching what Giannis Antetokounmpo did
item.description: Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images Giannis Antetokounmpo leaving the Milwaukee Bucks for the Miami Heat was the blockbuster deal of the summer. The Greek Freak spent over a decade with the Bucks, led them to an NBA championship and became one of the biggest superstars in the game during his time in Milwaukee. Yet, he chose not to shake hands with his old teammates recently, which shocked many people, including Draymond Green. Draymond Green reacts to Giannis Antetokounmpo snubbing former Bucks teammates Antetokounmpo faced the Milwaukee Bucks for the first time since his move to the Miami Heat, and he emerged victorious. The Heat won 137-130, with their big man scoring 27 points and recording 14 rebounds and nine assists in what was a scintillating display. After the game, Antetokounmpo was seen leaving the court without shaking hands with his former Bucks teammates. That was surprising, to say the least, not just for us fans but for fellow pros like Green as well. Speaking about the incident on his YouTube show, the Golden State Warriors star expressed his shock and suggested that there may have been some problems behind the scenes. He said: “A little surprised that Giannis ain’t shake the hands of any of his teammates. That was interesting to me, because those are guys that you’ve been going to war with. “And even if you don’t like something with the organisation, something that could’ve happened, you went to war with those guys. Giannis is one of those guys who brought his teammates to Greece. He’s a leader. “So to lead them guys and those guys followed your lead, and then to those very guys who followed his lead to now say nothing to them… “Unless something was going on in their locker room where he felt like guys turned their backs on him, which I’m not in their locker room, I don’t know. But I think that’s a little shocking. Like, that’s a little crazy to me.” We don’t know what Antetokounmpo’s relationship with the Bucks is like anymore, but he must be happy with his decision to leave Milwaukee. The Greek star has been brilliant with the Miami Heat, who, after a poor start, have begun to look like serious contenders. The Bucks, on the other hand, have won just one of their first 17 games and are at rock bottom in the Eastern Conference standings. item.description: FC Barcelona v Villarreal CF - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Barcelona manager Hansi Flick expressed deep frustration with the match officials following his side's dramatic 3-2 victory over Villarreal on Sunday. Despite witnessing a spirited comeback from two goals down, the German tactician was left fuming at the treatment his coaching staff received on the touchline. Flick vents fury at touchline scrutiny Flick did not hold back in his assessment of the officiating during Barcelona's narrow win over Villarreal , specifically targeting the conduct of the fourth official after being shown a yellow card for his protests and seeing substitute Fermin Lopez sent off from the bench in the 74th minute. According to referee Hernandez Hernandez's post-match report, the midfielder was dismissed for approaching the fourth official and protesting loudly, repeatedly saying 'Don't mess with me!', before heading straight down the tunnel prior to being shown the red card. 'The fourth official was only looking at our bench,' Flick stated during his post-match press conference. He expressed confusion over the lack of communication from the officiating crew, noting that he was sanctioned simply for asking questions about the game's flow. 'He has to help the referee on the field and he only looked at us. We will see what information they give us. I asked and they gave me a yellow card,' he said. The tension between the Barcelona bench and referee Hernandez Hernandez was a running theme throughout the afternoon. Flick admitted that the history and reputation of the officiating crew preceded the match, leading to an expectant but frustrated atmosphere. 'If it had been another result, maybe I wouldn't say anything, but today we knew which referee there was and we expected this. I am happy with the referees in general, but not with him. The linesman and the fourth official were very aware of us. You can do it differently, they could have talked to us, but they haven't told us anything,' the Blaugrana boss added. Early errors haunt the Blaugrana While the officiating was a major talking point, Flick was also quick to highlight the defensive lapses that saw Barcelona endure a catastrophic opening, conceding twice inside the first seven minutes through Thierno Barry and Tani Oluwaseyi - the first time the Blaugrana had shipped two goals that early in a league fixture since a clash with Real Zaragoza in November 1981. 'They got ahead in the first two plays. The first goal was a clear mistake of ours and they scored directly,' Flick remarked when analysing the nightmare start. item.title: Kirk Cousins on pace to make unique NFL history
item.description: Nov 24, 2022; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) warms up before the game against the New England Patriots at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-USA TODAY Sports Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins has had a whirlwind month, getting traded from the Las Vegas Raiders back to the franchise where he spent six seasons. Now, that midseason move has put the veteran in position to do something no quarterback has ever done before. Because the Raiders hadn’t yet had their bye week and the Vikings already had theirs, Cousins is on track to become the first quarterback in the modern era to play 18 regular-season games. So far, the 38-year-old reportedly has no objection to the unique opportunity to make NFL history. Cousins Returns to Minnesota The Vikings acquired Cousins from the Raiders just hours before this month’s NFL trade deadline, sending a 2027 third-round pick to Las Vegas in return. The deal brought the four-time Pro Bowler back to Minnesota, where he played from 2018 to 2023, and put him in line to start for the Vikings right away. It also cleared the way for No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza to take over as the starter in Las Vegas. Cousins had played the first nine games of the season for the Raiders while mentoring the rookie, and star wide receiver Justin Jefferson said that Cousins immediately took charge after rejoining the Vikings. His return got off to a strong start, too. Cousins threw for 207 yards and two touchdowns last Sunday as the Vikings rolled to a 30-10 win over the rival Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Across 10 combined games with Las Vegas and Minnesota, Cousins has completed 64.5% of his passes for 2,547 yards and 22 touchdowns. That has him sixth in the NFL in passing yards and tied with C.J. Stroud for second in touchdown passes, trailing only Joe Burrow’s 27. ‘Hasn’t had a bye week’ The Raiders don’t have their bye until Week 13, while the Vikings already had theirs back in Week 6. That leaves Cousins with no week off this season and a chance to suit up 18 times, starting with Sunday’s game against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City. That will allow Cousins to make some rather unique NFL history. No quarterback has ever played 18 regular-season games, but a handful of other players have. According to the Elias Sports Bureau, the only players to do it since 1930 are Leonard Williams (2023), Mike Williams (2024), Rashid Shaheed (2025), and Dre’Mont Jones (2025). Some teams have gone out of their way to avoid that situation. The Jacksonville Jaguars rested Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis last week after acquiring them from the Atlanta Falcons and Philadelphia Eagles, respectively, since both players would have otherwise lost their bye weeks. Cousins’ situation hasn’t gone unnoticed around the league, either. item.title: Real Madrid forward not guaranteed a starting spot under Mourinho despite encouraging signs
item.description: Real Madrid forward not guaranteed a starting spot under Mourinho despite encouraging signs In recent weeks, there has been a lot of noise surrounding Vinicius Jr. and his slow start to the season at Real Madrid. Coupled with the impressive performances of summer signing Yan Diomande, there have been question marks over the Brazilian international’s place in the starting lineup. But the 26-year-old seems to be recovering his form as he starred for Brazil during the recent international break and then impressed in his cameo in Real Madrid’s 2-1 win over Celta Vigo last night. No guaranteed spot for Vinicius However, despite the encouraging signs from Vinicius, Defensa Central reports that Jose Mourinho has no intention of restoring him to Real Madrid’s starting lineup simply because of his status at the club. Vinicius was left on the bench vs Celta Vigo. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Instead, the Portuguese tactician plans to rotate the superstar winger with Diomande on the left flank in both La Liga and the UEFA Champions League, with selection based on performances rather than reputation. Mourinho wants Vinicius to rediscover his peak form without interrupting Diomande’s development, particularly after the Ivorian’s impressive performances have made him a strong contender for regular minutes. There may also be occasions when the two wingers feature together, with Diomande moving to the right. Vinicius determined to win back his place Vinicius has been a regular starter for Real Madrid for several years and has already won major honours at the club. Being asked to share his position not something he is accustomed to. Vinicius will have to share minutes with Yan Diomande. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) However, Diomande has given Mourinho plenty of reasons to trust him, not only due to his attacking contributions, but also with the way he helps out the team off the ball. The Brazilian international is aware that his younger teammate has earned the trust of the manager and the support of the fans. But he remains determined to re-establish himself as a regular starter for Los Blancos . Vinicius understands what he needs to do to regain his place, with improvements needed in his physical condition while he works to regain his confidence following a difficult spell. For now, though, he will have to settle for sharing minutes with Diomande, as the coach plans on giving both players opportunities rather than guaranteeing either a place.

Draymond Green Slams Giannis Antetokounmpo Snubbing Former Bucks Teammates Speaking on his podcast, “ The Draymond Green Show ,” Green said he was “a little surprised that Giannis ain’t shake the hands of any of his teammates.” The game at Kaseya Center in Miami was Antetokounmpo’s first against Milwaukee since the Bucks traded him this summer. The two-time MVP won a championship in his 13 seasons with Milwaukee. Then Miami acquired him and Bobby Portis for Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel’el Ware, Kasparas Jakučionis, and a package of draft picks. Those years with the Bucks are at the center of Green’s objection. “Those are guys you been going to war with. Even if you don’t like something with the organization, you went to war with those guys,” he said. He is a leader. So to lead them guys, and for those guys to follow your lead, and then those very guys that followed your lead now say nothing to them…” He finished the thought with a caveat, though he still landed on the criticism: “…unless something was going on in their locker room where he felt like guys turned their back on him… but I think that’s a little shocking, that’s a little crazy to me.” Asked after the game whether the overhaul of Milwaukee’s roster and coaching staff played a part in how he carried himself that night, Antetokounmpo described his approach to game days. “Look, I think since I was a kid, when I play basketball I try to lock in as much as I can. People that have been around me know how I operate on game days. I try not to say much. I try not to interact as much. The only thing in my mind is ‘how can I help my team win and how can I do my job?’ It doesn’t matter who I play. I could have been playing against my four brothers and my two sons,” he said. item.title: Chiefs Elevate Two Players As O-Line Woes Deepen
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs made a move to shore up their depth. According to Arrowhead Pride, Nate Carter and Pete Nygra were promoted from the practice squad by the team for Sunday’s game versus the Arizona Cardinals. Kenneth Walker remains out with a groin injury, and Trey Smith is ruled out due to concussion protocol. The team needs depth and stability on the line because the starters are unavailable. Reid’s Lineup Dilemma Head coach Andy Reid admitted the situation is fluid and compared the upcoming decisions to a preseason game. “Well, we’ve got a variety there, but they’re all going to have a shot to get in there and go,” Reid said on Friday. The coach also noted that the team has confidence in backup Mike Caliendo if he gets the start. “So, we’ll see how it all goes, but I think everybody has a lot of trust in Mike (Caliendo) if he’s the one in there playing,” he added. Yet, the presence of Nygra suggests the team might be looking elsewhere. Longtime radio host Tim Grunhard reported on Saturday that Hunter Nourzad could start at right guard instead, casting doubt on Caliendo’s role. A Rookie’s Big Moment Pete Nygra gets his first chance to play in the NFL, but the timing is risky. The 6-foot-4, 300-pound undrafted rookie out of Louisville has been on the practice squad all season, per A to Z Sports . He is now the primary backup interior lineman with the flexibility to play both guard and center. Because Jaylon Moore is also unavailable, the whole right side of the offensive line remains uncertain. The Chiefs are forced to experiment with their lineup against a Cardinals team that just upgraded their quarterback situation by starting 40-year-old Josh Johnson. The final injury report confirmed that Moore, Smith, and Walker all missed practice on Friday. “The guys who didn’t practice today were Jaylon Moore, Trey Smith, and Ken Walker,” Reid said. “All of which are improving.” Reid confirmed all three are out for the game. The Chiefs will face the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET at Arrowhead Stadium.

item.title: Thunder Face Injury Crisis As Heat Streak Continues
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Oklahoma City Thunder face a massive test on Sunday night against the Miami Heat. The team must deal with an injury list that now includes eight players. Heavy.com reported that reigning two-time NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is listed as questionable. He is dealing with a lower back contusion and neck strain. This news comes just after he poured in 40 points against the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday. The Heat enter the game with the longest active winning streak in the entire league. Miami has won six games in a row heading into this matchup at the Kaseya Center. Key Players Sit Out The injury report released on Saturday shows a deep roster hit. Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, and Cason Wallace are all ruled out for the game. Holmgren is still recovering from a partially torn patellar tendon with a potential return next month. J-Dub and Wallace are just starting their rehab process from separate surgeries on their left ankle and left shoulder. Right hip soreness will cause Alex Caruso to sit out his second consecutive game. Jaylin Williams sits out with low back spasms, marking the eighth time he has missed a game in his last ten. Thomas Sorber and Nikola Topic have no timetable for their return. The sheer number of sidelined players highlights a rough season for the Thunder. Depth Under Fire With so many stars on the bench, the team’s depth is being tested in real time. The positions vacated by injured starters have been filled by Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain. They must step up immediately against a Miami squad that is on a hot streak. Following a grueling 126-120 victory against the Pelicans, the Thunder are now rested. That victory came during the 2026 NBA Cup. Now the focus shifts to survival on the road. The team begins a two-game trip on Sunday against the Heat. Heavy.com noted the game takes place amid the GTA VI craze in Miami. Final Status Check Shai Gilgeous-Alexander will be re-evaluated before tip-off on Sunday. He could be upgraded to available status if his neck and back feel better. The rest of the eight players listed are confirmed out for the night. This leaves the Thunder with a thin rotation against a confident opponent. The Heat have not lost a game in their last six attempts.

It is just as well for Dundee United that the Iraq international is tied to them until at least the summer, his early season appearances for Utrecht ruling out a transfer during the January window. item.title: Why was Leny Yoro sent off against Liverpool?
item.description: Life at Manchester United got off to a nightmare start for Mauricio Pochettino as his side was reduced to 10 men inside eight minutes in his managerial bow against Liverpool . Liverpool started brightly and fashioned a chance out of nothing when Ronald Araujo’s hooked clearance left Matthijs de Ligt - making his first league start in a year - in no man’s land. Follow live - Pochettino off to nightmare start as Man Utd manager at Liverpool Alexander Isak latched onto the ball but was clattered into last man Leny Yoro just outside the box, prompting referee Sam Barrett to reach into his pocket and show the Frenchman a red card. Leny Yoro saw red in the early stages of Man United’s clash with Liverpool (PA) "It doesn't matter if you're playing with a back four, or back five, you've got to do the basics right. De Ligt - I'm amazed with him at this level,” Roy Keane said on Sky Sports. "I know he's come back from an injury, he's just not reading the flight of the ball. If you do get it wrong, you run back, you sprint back, and then Yoro has got to be covering. If you're a defender, you always expect the worst." There was a debate over whether VAR should have overturned the decision due to Isak’s heavy touch, which put into question he would have kept control of the ball - a key consideration in determining if a player has denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity (DOGSO). "Isak's not getting the ball. There's no way he's getting the ball,” Keane added. "It's clumsy from United. Obviously it's one straight ball over the top. You shouldn't be in so much trouble. "But there's no way he's getting that ball. Absolutely not. I know Isak is quick and he's sharp, but we've looked at it again. "It's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger. But Isak is not getting that ball. Absolutely not." But VAR John Brooks did not call for a review, with the Premier League Match Centre writing in a statement: “The referee’s call of red card to Yoro for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO) was checked and confirmed by VAR. Yoro leaves the pitch after being sent off for Man United (Getty) “REF: ‘It's a red card for DOGSO. On-field decision is outside [the box], red card, DOGSO’. “VAR: ‘Defender bundles into him into the back, gets too tight, I think it's a foul’.” Things then went from bad to worse for United as Dominik Szoboszlai stepped up to the free-kick and fired past Senne Lammens into the bottom-left corner, ensuring Yoro’s blunder was fully punished. Liverpool doubled their lead just three minutes later, with Florian Wirtz volleying high into the goal as Pochettino’s side rapidly unravelled. Liverpool’s outright domination of the opening stages, combined with losing a defender, sparked Pochettino into making an early change, replacing forward Bryan Mbeumo with centre-back Harry Maguire in the 22nd minute.

item.title: Fox Sports makes donation to Ferris State after 'Big Noon Kickoff'
item.description: Fox Sports left a mark on Ferris State. It also left a check. "Big Noon Kickoff" aired live from the campus in Big Rapids, Mich., on Saturday, Nov. 21, to kick off the start of the Division II playoffs, and the start of Ferris State's drive for a third consecutive national championship. During the two-hour show, Fox Sports also announced a $50,000 donation to the school's athletic department. The donation will go toward the planned future Indoor Activities Complex. The $61.7-million project is scheduled to be constructed in two phases over the next several years, assuming the school meets its ambitious fundraising goal. Fox Sports said its donation will fund a media room at the athletic complex. It will be called the Fox Sports Media Room, and, according to the network, go toward "supporting the next generation of sports storytellers." The donation was among many highlights Saturday, when Ferris State became the first Division II school to host one of college football's premier pregame television shows. A crowd in the thousands lined up early, before sunrise, and was boisterous throughout the show. Many Fox Sports employees called the visit to Big Rapids one of their favorite stops since the show debuted in 2019. "What an awesome day and such a historic day for Ferris State University and Big Rapids," Ferris State head coach Tony Annese said following the Bulldogs' 45-14 win over Missouri-based Truman State before a crowd of more than 8,000. "The credit goes to the students who showed up big, our fans, the staff and the community for supporting us so well." Fox Sports, with the "Big Noon Kickoff" cast including Urban Meyer, Mark Ingram II, Brady Quinn, Matt Leinart, host Rob Stone and reporter Chris Fallica, shined a key spotlight on Ferris State, a small school with an enrollment just under 10,000, and Big Rapids, a city that has a full-time population of even less than that. School administrators hope the spotlight will help spur donations toward the new athletic complex. The first phase of the project is set to include a 134,000-square-foot indoor facility, with a track and training space for all of the school's sports. That includes a football practice field. Additional parking lots are part of the project. The second phase of the project is set to include stadium improvements, including Top Taggart Field lighting, turf and bleachers replacements, plus a 42,000-square-foot support building that will house locker rooms, training space, coaches' offices, fan suites and meeting rooms. In announcing the project earlier this year, Ferris State officials said: "This is more than a facilities upgrade. It’s an investment in people — our student-athletes, our fans, our community." The athletic department added: "Championship culture drives momentum. And momentum demands investment." A BIG NOON visit with a lasting impact. ❤️ @FOXSports is proud to contribute $50,000 toward the new athletics facility at @FerrisState , including a FOX Sports Media Room

item.description: Report: Juventus, Milan and Napoli on alert as Chelsea open door to Palestra exit Chelsea are prepared to let Marco Palestra leave as Xabi Alonso pushes to sign Jules Koundé from Barcelona, and Juventus, Milan and Napoli are all interested in bringing the full-back back to Italy. According to El Nacional , Alonso is in favour of signing Koundé soon, even in January. The Chelsea coach is willing to let the Italian leave, as he has offers to return to Serie A from clubs such as Juventus, AC Milan and SSC Napoli, and bring in Koundé in exchange. The full-back was named Serie A Defender of the Year for 2025/26, on loan at Cagliari, but has struggled for minutes at Chelsea. The Blues paid Atalanta around €60m for him in the summer. A thigh injury delayed his Chelsea debut until October, and El Nacional puts him at 202 minutes across six matches. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team.
